title: One More Step Toward Peace
description: An Ethics and Leadership Teaching Stone episode about Vietnam, the temptation of escalation and the people who bear its cost. Historical-fiction dialogue, seven choices, four knowledge questions, and a separate Decision Note. 10–12 minutes plus the check.

label classroomOpening
scene classroom
I: I rest my hand on the Teaching Stone. In my notebook I have written a question: when does protecting someone become an excuse to keep putting them in danger?
I: The stone warms. Vietnam, mid-1968. American troops fight alongside South Vietnam’s forces against North Vietnamese and southern revolutionary forces, supported by China and the Soviet Union. The Tet Offensive has shaken American confidence. Peace talks have begun in Paris, but the fighting continues.

quiz.prompt: Which description best explains the proxy-war element in Vietnam?
options: Outside powers supported Vietnamese forces pursuing their own goals, alongside direct foreign intervention.
Vietnamese people had no objectives until outside powers gave them orders.
No outside country used its own combat forces.
The documents show that all participants shared one objective.
quiz.explanation: Outside sponsorship and direct intervention coexisted. Vietnamese actors retained their own purposes; the proxy label does not explain the entire war.

quiz.prompt: Why could escalation appear attractive to McNamara in 1965?
options: It guaranteed a quick victory with no civilian cost.
It promised to defend an ally and improve bargaining leverage, despite acknowledged risks.
He had evidence that the opposing side could never respond.
The documents show that all participants shared one objective.
quiz.explanation: The argument involved protection, credibility and leverage. The acknowledged possibility of a larger stalemate shows that the promised result was uncertain.

quiz.prompt: What does encountering Trâm through her diary help us understand?
options: One diary proves what every Vietnamese person believed.
Humanizing her requires ignoring her revolutionary commitment.
A political opponent can have agency, convictions, relationships and a complex inner life.
The documents show that all participants shared one objective.
quiz.explanation: Her perspective is particular, not universal. Understanding someone’s humanity neither requires agreement nor removes their political commitments.

quiz.prompt: What do the 1968 records presented here establish?
options: The war definitely would have ended that year without interference.
Campaign contacts encouraged South Vietnam to delay participation; the alternative outcome remains uncertain.
Every negotiating party had already accepted a complete peace agreement.
The documents show that all participants shared one objective.
quiz.explanation: The records document efforts to delay participation. They cannot establish a certain counterfactual peace settlement or the asserted private bargain.
